'''Kurt Mahler''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name="frs">{{Cite journal | last1 = Coates | first1 = J. H. | last2 = Van Der Poorten | first2 = A. J. | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.1994.0016 | title = Kurt Mahler. 26 July 1903-26 February 1988 | journal = [[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 39 | pages = 264 | year = 1994 | issue = 39 | doi-access = free }}</ref> (26 July 1903 – 25 February 1988) was a German mathematician who worked in the fields of [[transcendental number theory]], [[diophantine approximation]], [[p-adic analysis|''p''-adic analysis]], and the [[geometry of numbers]].<ref name="frs"/><ref name="carma">[https://carmamaths.org/resources/mahler/biography.html The Kurt Mahler Archive] available from CARMA research center at carmamaths.org</ref>

==Career==
Mahler was a student at the universities in [[Frankfurt]] and [[Göttingen]], graduating with a [[Ph.D.]] from [[Johann Wolfgang Goethe University of Frankfurt am Main]] in 1927; his advisor was [[Carl Ludwig Siegel]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=34223}}</ref>
He left Germany with the rise of [[Adolf Hitler]] and accepted an invitation by [[Louis Mordell]] to go to [[Manchester]]. However, at the start of [[World War II]] he was interned as an [[enemy alien]] in Central Camp in [[Douglas, Isle of Man|Douglas]], [[Isle of Man]], where he met [[Kurt Hirsch]], although he was released after only three months.<ref>[http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Biographies/Mahler.html Biography of Kurt Mahler] available from www.educ.fc.ul.pt</ref> He became a British citizen in 1946.

Mahler held the following positions:
*[[University of Groningen]]
** Assistant 1934–1936
*[[University of Manchester]]
** Assistant Lecturer at 1937–1939, 1941–1944
** Lecturer, 1944–1947; Senior Lecturer, 1948–1949; Reader, 1949–1952
** Professor of Mathematical Analysis, 1952–1963
* Professor of Mathematics, Institute of Advanced Studies, [[Australian National University]], 1963–1968 and 1972–1975
* Professor of Mathematics, [[Ohio State University]], USA, 1968–1972
* [[Professor Emeritus]], [[Australian National University]], from 1975.

==Research==
Mahler worked in a broad variety of mathematical disciplines, including [[transcendental number theory]], [[diophantine approximation]], [[p-adic analysis|''p''-adic analysis]], and the [[geometry of numbers]].<ref name="frs"/><ref name="carma"/>

Mahler proved that the [[Prouhet–Thue–Morse constant]] and the [[Champernowne constant]] {{math|0.1234567891011121314151617181920}}... are [[transcendental number]]s.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Mahler | first1=Kurt | title=Arithmetische Eigenschaften der Lösungen einer Klasse von Funktionalgleichungen | journal=Math. Annalen | volume=101 | date=1929 | pages=342–366| doi=10.1007/BF01454845 | url=https://carmamaths.org/resources/mahler/docs/004.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Mahler | first1=Kurt | title=Arithmetische Eigenschaften einer Klasse von Dezimalbrüchen | journal=Proc. Konin. Neder. Akad. Wet. | volume=40 | date=1937 | pages=421–428 | url=https://carmamaths.org/resources/mahler/docs/046.pdf }}</ref>

Mahler was the first to give an explicit [[irrationality measure]] for {{math|''π''}}, in 1953 (of {{math|42}}).<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Mahler | first1=Kurt | title=On the approximation of π | journal=Nederl. Akad. Wetensch. Proc. Ser. A. | volume=56 | date=1953 | pages=342–366 | url=https://carmamaths.org/resources/mahler/docs/119.pdf }}</ref><ref name="Pi Source Book ">{{cite book | last1=Berggren | first1=Lennart | last2=Borwein | first2=Jonathan M. | last3=Borwein | first3=Peter B. | last4=Mahler | first4=Kurt | title=Pi, a source book | publisher=Springer | publication-place=New York | date=2004 | isbn=0-387-20571-3 | oclc=53814116 | pages=306–318}}</ref> Although some have suggested the irrationality measure of {{math|''π''}} is likely to be {{math|2}}, the current best estimate is {{math|7.103205334137}}…, due to [[Doron Zeilberger]] and [[Wadim Zudilin]].<ref name="Zeilberger Zudilin irrationality measure">{{cite journal | last1=Zeilberger | first1=Doron | last2=Zudilin | first2=Wadim | title=The irrationality measure of {{math|''π''}} is at most {{math|7.103205334137}}… | journal=Moscow Journal of Combinatorics and Number Theory | publisher=Mathematical Sciences Publishers | volume=9 | issue=4 | date=2020-11-05 | issn=2640-7361 | doi=10.2140/moscow.2020.9.407 | pages=407–419| arxiv=1912.06345 | s2cid=209370638 }}</ref>

==Awards==
He was elected a fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1948<ref name="frs"/> and a fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]] in 1965. He was awarded the [[London Mathematical Society]]'s [[Senior Berwick Prize]] in 1950, the [[De Morgan Medal]], 1971, and the [[Thomas Ranken Lyle Medal]], 1977.<ref name="frs"/>

==Personal life==
Mahler spoke [[Chinese language|Chinese]] and was an expert photographer.<ref name="frs"/>
